RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Skyler Iverson
Member ID: W313340363
Reference Number: POC-30230D15F4-69823
Requested Service: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-18
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-14

To the Comagine Health Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (CPT 22551), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and I am submitting this appeal along with the clinical documentation summarized below, which I believe directly addresses that concern.

I want to be transparent about the basis for this appeal: I have located the document that Comagine Health identifies as governing this determination — the Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (referred to by Comagine as "AKM CSSC") — on Comagine Health's provider resource site. The only text from that source I am able to quote directly is Comagine's own description of the document: "This document contains information and criteria applied to cervical spine surgery requests for degenerative cervical spine disease." I was not able to obtain the full text of the specific medical-necessity criteria (e.g., the specific imaging, exam, and conservative-care elements) contained within that document, so I am not quoting or attributing any further specific policy language to Comagine Health or Alaska Medicaid in this letter. The clinical arguments below are made in my own words and by my treating surgeon, mapped to the general categories of evidence (imaging correlation, neurologic findings, and failed conservative care) that are typically required to support medical necessity for cervical fusion. I am formally requesting that Comagine Health provide me and my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, with the complete text of the specific criteria/pathway applied to this denial so that we may respond to it point by point if this appeal is not granted on the record below.

Why the imaging and clinical record support medical necessity:

1. Imaging findings correlate directly with my symptoms and exam findings.
   My cervical MRI, performed 2026-06-28, shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This is not an incidental or asymptomatic finding: it corresponds precisely to my clinical presentation of right-sided radicular pain and numbness into the thumb and index finger — the classic C6 dermatomal distribution — together with corresponding weakness. On examination, provocative testing was positive on the affected side, and I have a documented neurologic deficit at the level shown on imaging. In other words, the imaging finding is not an isolated radiographic abnormality; it is corroborated by a matching neurologic exam and a matching symptom pattern, which is the core clinical correlation that imaging-based medical necessity review is intended to confirm.

2. I have completed and failed an adequate trial of conservative care.
   - I have had 12 months of progressive neck pain that has not improved with rest.
   - I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-05-06 through 2026-07-01, 20 visits), including cervical traction and postural training, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
   - I was treated with NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
   - I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-06, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned.
   This is a substantial, well-documented course of non-operative treatment across multiple modalities (physical therapy, medication, and injection) that has failed to resolve my pain, numbness, and weakness.

3. There are no contraindications to surgery.
   I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker. There is no clinical factor in my record that would counsel against proceeding with surgery.

4. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has recommended this procedure based on the correlation between my imaging, exam, and symptoms, and after conservative care failed to provide lasting relief.

Given this record — twelve months of symptoms, a clearly corresponding structural lesion on MRI, a matching neurologic deficit and positive provocative testing, and a documented, multi-modality failed conservative treatment course — I ask that Comagine Health reverse the denial and approve CPT 22551 as medically necessary.

I am requesting the following as part of this appeal:
1. Reversal of the denial and approval of the requested cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551.
2. A copy of the complete Alaska Medicaid Cervical Spine Surgery Criteria (AKM CSSC), including the specific criteria, pathway, or subset applied to my case, so that my surgeon and I can respond to any specific element not already addressed above.
3. Written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the date by which a decision will be issued.

Enclosed with this letter, please find:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-06 to 2026-07-01)
- Medication and injection records
- MRI cervical spine report, 2026-06-28
- Office notes documenting neurologic exam and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, MD

Please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address] if any additional information is needed. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14, and I am submitting it well in advance of that date. I also ask that you advise me in writing whether a separate, shorter deadline applies to any subsequent State Fair Hearing request, as I want to preserve all of my appeal rights.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Skyler Iverson
Member ID: W313340363
[Date]
